preamble: In Sotho-Tswana, root-initial /r/ hardens to the aspirated stop [tʰ] in post-nasal contexts, part of a broader post-nasal fortition that also turns /l/ into [t], /f/ into [pʰ] and /s/ into [tsʰ]. Northern Sotho shows the pattern: rata 'love' gives reflexive ithata 'love oneself' and nthata 'love me' with the 1st person singular object prefix.

examples.note: The reflexive prefix i- changes root-initial r to aspirated th; Prinsloo lists this among reflexives with sound change but no semantic shift.
The 1st person singular object prefix N- triggers the same hardening, alongside l > t (lebala > itebala/ntebala) and f > ph (fahla > iphahla/mphahla).

sources: Prinsloo, D. J. (1992). Lemmatization of Reflexives in Northern Sotho. Lexikos 2. https://doi.org/10.5788/2-1-1133
